property_summary: A zero-value deposit call does not revert (assert in P prevents overflow but should allow zero), so deposit should never revert for any sender and any msg.value >= 0 in P — but the mutant's changed assert can cause a revert on zero-value deposit in some circumstances.

After a deposit of a positive value, the caller's recorded balance strictly increases by at least that value (i.e. balances[msg.sender] after deposit >= old balance + value).
Calling deposit with any nonzero wei value must not revert (i.e., deposit always succeeds for any caller and value).
Depositing zero wei may revert (original requires assert preventing overflow on nonzero sums), but depositing a positive amount must not revert in the original; thus reverted is true iff amount == 0.
For any deposit amount, deposit reverts exactly when the amount is zero (i.e., positive deposits never revert while zero deposit may revert).
deposit reverts only when adding value would overflow the caller's recorded balance (i.e., when balances[msg.sender] + amount <= balances[msg.sender]); otherwise it does not revert.

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit value, after deposit() returns the contract's recorded balances[msg.sender] strictly increases by the sent amount; removing the assert allows an overflow edge-case (when balances[msg.sender] + msg.value wraps to <= balances[msg.sender]) to break this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor address and any deposit amount in uint256, after deposit() returns the recorded balances[depositor] is equal to its previous value plus the deposited amount (i.e. balances increases by exactly msg.value); removing the assert allows a wrapping overflow so for some depositor and amount the mutant's balances does not equal previous + amount.

For any depositor address and deposit amount where the depositor's prior balance is at most uint256 max - amount, calling deposit(msg.value) never reverts and increases the depositor's recorded balance by exactly the sent amount; removing the assert allows a wraparound case where the deposit can cause the sum to overflow and either not increase as expected (or potentially revert on some environments), so the mutant fails for some inputs where prior balance + amount would overflow.

For every depositor and deposit amount, after a successful deposit the contract's stored balance for that depositor is >= the previous stored balance (i.e., deposit cannot decrease the recorded balance); removing the assert in the mutant allows a uint256 overflow that can make the post-deposit stored balance be < pre-deposit for some inputs.
After calling deposit(amount) with amount>0, the contract balance increases by that amount (address(c).balance == old_balance + amount).

property_summary: For any caller and any positive deposit amount, calling deposit() on the correct contract increases the contract's recorded balance for that caller (balances[msg.sender] after call >= before + value) and the buggy mutant inverts the assert causing positive-value deposits to revert (so for some inputs deposit() will fail or not increase the recorded balance).

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount that they send, the correct contract accepts the deposit (call succeeds) and increases the contract's balance (address(c).balance increases by that amount); the mutant inverts the assert so some positive deposits revert (call fails) and thus fail to increase address(c).balance.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount, after calling deposit() the contract's internal recorded balances[msg.sender] equals the sum of all successful deposits made by that caller (i.e., balances never decrease and when a deposit succeeds it strictly increases by the sent value); the mutant's inverted assert causes positive-value deposits to revert (or not behave) so there exist inputs where this invariant is violated.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount, if the deposit transaction does NOT revert then the caller's recorded balance (balances[msg.sender]) strictly increases by the sent amount; the mutant's inverted assert makes some positive-value deposits revert, so there exist inputs where a non-reverting deposit would be required but the mutant reverts, violating the universal rule about: 'if deposit call returns success then recorded balance increased by amount'.

For every caller and nonzero amount, if deposit() returns successfully then the contract's recorded balances[msg.sender] strictly increases by the sent amount; the mutant inverts the assert causing some positive deposits to revert (so there exist inputs where a successful deposit cannot occur), violating that universal relation between a successful deposit call and the per-caller balance increase.
After two deposits by the same sender, the contract balance for that sender is at least the sum of the two deposit amounts (i.e., deposits accumulate).
A successful deposit call should never revert (i.e., deposit should always succeed for any msg.value > 0).

After a deposit of amount x by an address a, a subsequent deposit of amount y by the same address cannot reduce the contract's balance held for a (i.e., balance for a after second deposit is >= first deposit amount).

For any sender and two sequential deposits by the same caller, if the first deposit succeeded then the second deposit cannot revert when sending a nonzero amount (i.e., successful first deposit implies second deposit with any positive value also succeeds).

For any caller, after a successful deposit of some nonzero amount, a subsequent deposit of any nonzero amount will not cause the caller's observable outcome (whether the second call reverts) to be true when the first succeeded — i.e., if the first deposit succeeded then the second deposit also succeeds for any positive value.

For any caller and any positive deposit value, calling deposit() increases that caller's recorded balance by at least the sent amount (i.e., balance_new >= balance_old + msg.value); the mutant overwrites the balance with msg.value and thus can violate this for callers with existing balances.

For any depositor and any nonzero deposit amount, after a deposit the recorded balance is at least the deposit amount (i.e., balances[actor] >= amount); the mutant that overwrites instead of adding can make the balance smaller than a previous accumulation and thus violate this when the actor had a prior balance and deposits a smaller/new amount, so the mutant can produce balances < amount.

For any actor and any two sequential deposits (first amount a, then amount b), the reference contract ensures the recorded balance after the second deposit equals the previous balance plus b (i.e., it accumulates: balance_after == balance_before + b); the mutant that overwrites with msg.value breaks this when the second deposit is made, producing balance_after == b instead of balance_before + b.
